title: Watch: US strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers after Iran targets 2 navy warships
content: In a tense confrontation, US forces targeted three Iranian oil tankers after missile strikes on Navy warships. The vessels successfully dodged multiple Iranian attacks without any injuries reported. Serving as financial support for Iran's Revolutionary Guard and proxies, one tanker was rendered useless near Kharg Island, while another faced destruction close to Jask, with the last one obliterated in the Gulf of Oman as its crew evacuated.

title: Putin orders 3-day pause in strikes on Kyiv as US delegation arrives in Russia
content: US special representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow for crucial peace talks. President Putin ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv for the American delegation's visit. Both Russia and Ukraine had intensified long-range attacks before this diplomatic engagement. The US push aims to revive efforts to end the ongoing conflict between the nations. The envoys will travel to Ukraine after concluding their discussions in Russia.

title: ‘No handshake’ again: Harmanpreet, Fatima avoid customary gesture at Asia Cup toss
content: The long-standing no-handshake tradition persisted between the captains of India and Pakistan during the Asia Cup match. In Dubai, Fatima Sana won the toss and elected to bat first. Notably, Harmanpreet Kaur marked her 150th T20I match as captain. With both teams already in the semi-finals, India's aim remains to uphold their dominance over Pakistan.

title: ‘Don’t give me these useless jumlas’: Kangana pulls up officials over unused funds
content: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut expressed anger over delayed development works. She questioned the utilization of nearly eleven crore rupees allocated for projects. Officials had repeatedly assured her that funds were being used effectively. However, external surveys revealed a different and concerning reality on the ground. Ranaut demanded immediate completion of pending works and accountability from officials.

title: As data center costs rise, Meta is using robots to plug cables & reset servers
content: Meta is reportedly testing robots for physical tasks within its data centers. These robots could potentially handle cable plugging and server resets, among other duties.  The company is evaluating robotic arms for power cycling and cable swapping operations.  This initiative aims to reduce labor costs as AI infrastructure spending increases.  Meta spokesperson Francis Brennan stated the company is hiring and training more workers.

title: Where have all the buyers gone? DC homes lose value as demand dries up
content: In Washington, the housing market is revealing an intriguing dynamic, with many properties available at discounted rates—almost one-fifth of homes listed currently are priced lower than what they were purchased for initially. This development points to a slump in buyer interest instead of a surplus of homes for sale. Luxury regions may see upward price trajectories, yet affordable condos are struggling.

title: Canadian billionaire Kevin O’Leary says success requires sacrifice, focus and obsession
content: Kevin O'Leary emphasizes that reaching peak success requires immense dedication and sacrifice. He recommends that individuals focus on three to five key priorities while steering clear of distractions. Influential figures like Mark Cuban and Elon Musk echo similar sentiments, highlighting the role of sacrifice in amassing wealth. O'Leary cautions entrepreneurs to acknowledge failures swiftly, as pouring more resources into failing ideas rarely leads to redemption.

title: ‘Always in chaos’: Hayden’s blunt verdict on Pakistan cricket amid latest turmoil
content: Matthew Hayden, the former Australian cricket opener, shared his insights on the persistent instability within Pakistan cricket. He emphasised how this ongoing chaos hampers players' ability to perform consistently. Despite Pakistan's wealth of natural talent, Hayden argued that the country's issues hinder its chances to harness that potential into becoming a cricketing powerhouse on the global stage.

title: 33-year-old buys 81-room Arkansas hotel for $2.55m and spends $1.1m rebuilding
content: From a modest beginning, Greg Clark has embarked on an impressive journey in the hospitality sector, currently breathing new life into an eighty-one-room hotel located in the picturesque Eureka Springs. His aim is to craft exceptional guest experiences, showcasing his renovation progress on TikTok. With a vision to build ten carefully curated hotels over seven years, Clark's journey is one of ambition and creativity.

title: 14,800 plastic bottles built one model house; project later grew to 15 homes
content: In an inspiring initiative, Nigerian engineer Yahaya Ahmed is turning discarded plastic bottles into sustainable building materials. To date, he has constructed around fifteen houses utilizing this creative technique. This process cuts down construction costs and offers superior insulation properties. By filling empty bottles with sand, Ahmed effectively combats plastic waste while providing cost-effective and durable housing alternatives.

title: Jeff Bezos' ex-wife sets new record with donations to historically Black colleges
content: MacKenzie Scott has now donated over one billion dollars to historically Black colleges. Her recent forty-two million dollar gift to Elizabeth City State University marked this milestone. Scott has provided significant funding to numerous institutions since 2020. These unrestricted donations empower universities to allocate funds as needed. Her extensive philanthropic efforts support various educational and community initiatives.

title: Son loses gifted flat after neglecting parents; why he may still inherit it later
content: A recent Bombay High Court case involved a son who was directed to vacate his father’s flat after the court found that he had failed to honour the condition attached to the gift of the property. The flat had been transferred to him on the understanding that he would take care of his parents, an obligation he did not fulfil.

title: Messi and Ronaldo could finally play together for first time after special invite

Tevez hopes to reunite the longtime rivals as teammates for one night, alongside legends including Rooney, Scholes, Pirlo, Ferdinand, Vidic, Buffon and Van der Sar. The Argentine says he is confident he can persuade both superstars to attend.

title: Travis Kelce expands his business empire with a $53M hydration deal

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end highlighted the importance of quality hydration for peak performance and recovery. The move added to his partnerships across fashion, fitness, food and lifestyle brands. At the same time, Kelce remained focused on football, making it clear that winning another Super Bowl was his biggest goal.

title: Naomi Osaka vs Serena Williams: How did their 2018 US Open final change her career?
content: Naomi Osaka made history in 2018 by winning her first Grand Slam title against Serena Williams. This pivotal match showcased her exceptional composure, turning what could have been a tumultuous finale into a career-defining moment. Her triumph set the stage for her ascent as a preeminent figure in tennis and a celebrated athlete from Japan, earning her admiration worldwide and paving the way for more significant victories.

As the national Test team battles in the World Test Championship standings, these issues continue to mount.

He was rushed to Malvani General Hospital for immediate medical attention.  However, hospital authorities later confirmed the boy was declared brought dead. title: Kimi Antonelli heads into Monza GP as first Italian championship leader since 1953

title: Lorry hits BRS president KT Rama Rao’s car in Telangana

The BRS leader was inside the car and escaped the incident unhurt. The accident caused slight damage to the car door and brief panic. CSK must also navigate the future of their coaching staff and the legendary MS Dhoni.

title: DTC fought conductor for 32 years over Rs 67, now fined Rs 1 lakh by Delhi HC
content: The Delhi High Court has imposed a fine of one lakh rupees on the Delhi Transport Corporation for its relentless pursuit of a thirty-two-year-old legal battle involving a bus conductor. The court criticized the drawn-out litigation as an abuse of the legal system. The conductor had been seeking seventeen months of unpaid wages following his dismissal, while the court dismissed DTC's challenge to a tribunal ruling.

title: ‘Stop the boats’: Masked men block roads to Dover port in anti-immigration protest
content: Masked men blocked roads leading to Britain's busiest ferry port in Dover. This protest disrupted traffic around the major cross-Channel hub on Saturday morning. Port officials stated that all traffic in and out of the port had been stopped. Videos showed several dozen men dressed in black, shouting "stop the boats". The incident appeared to be an anti-immigration protest, causing significant traffic jams.

title: Sachin honours his 'first teacher' father Ramesh with fellowship for young doctors

This fellowship focuses on cleft and craniofacial care specialization, fostering his father's legacy of education as a means of opportunity. Additionally, Tendulkar's foundation promotes initiatives in sports, healthcare, and children's education.

title: Goa compensates artists with homes destroyed by natural calamities; here's how
content: The Kritadnyata Nidhi scheme in Goa is a boon for artists, providing up to Rs 25,000 for home repairs following disasters. Artists must be Goan citizens, aged fifty or older, with a family income below two lakh rupees to qualify. This welfare initiative extends support to medical needs and various artist services. Notably, age restrictions can be adjusted for those with specific needs or circumstances.

title: NIA court convicts 10 in 2013 Jhiram Valley Maoist attack case

The court reserved the quantum of punishment for September sixteenth. Statements from one hundred and one witnesses were recorded during the trial proceedings. Defence lawyers plan to appeal the verdict in a higher court.

title: Iraq’s petrol problem deepens as OPEC member hit by Hormuz disruption
content: Iraq is grappling with severe petrol shortages as long lines of vehicles form at fuel stations. Ongoing regional conflicts are hindering essential fuel imports, disrupting tanker movement through the vital Strait of Hormuz. The nation heavily relies on these imports to offset domestic production gaps, leading to panic buying and further complicating supply issues. In response, the government is actively seeking additional fuel shipments to replenish reserves.

The proposed centers are intended to operate within international legal frameworks.

title: Beyond the big four: Why Indian students are preferring Europe?
content: The trend of Indian students pursuing higher education in Continental Europe is on the rise, with Germany taking the forefront, especially in engineering and STEM fields. France and Italy are becoming preferred choices for students interested in business and design. Accessible tuition fees, along with favorable post-study work options, significantly attract these students. Nevertheless, housing and language fluency are crucial factors influencing their success.
